newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs trade $1.00 lower - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs trade $1.00 lower - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs traded at least a $1.00 per cwt lower at interior markets Thursday, with continued declines in cash pork prices driving hog prices down, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa-southern Minnesota dealers reported early trades at $52.50 per cwt at country points and $53.50 delivered to packing plants. In Illinois, tops were $54.00 in the country and $55.00 at the plants.
Indiana hogs traded $1.00 lower early from $52.00 to $52.50 at country points, but dealers continued to buy hogs after dropping bids to $51.50 to $52.00, sources there said.
Hog dealers said most major packers were scheduled to run full production shifts Thursday and Friday, but not slaughter Saturday.
Despite the sharp drop in hog prices this week, hog marketings remained robust. Some dealers said producers appear to be willing sellers as long as hog prices are in the 50's.
"The numbers are still there," said an Iowa dealer. "They (packers) are getting all they want."
USDA reported pork cutout values late Wednesday were down $0.81 to $0.66 per cwt with grade 1 carcasses at $75.10 versus $80.59 a week ago.
